HOWEVER: 1 MAJOR codepoint-semantic drift on 0x647b reuse, 1 MAJOR production-hot-path call to a `_for_test`-named test-API, and 3 MINOR findings (NF-4 strip-test actually exercises AAD-mutation not NF-4 verify; pure-PQ encrypt+decrypt paths are structurally unreachable; KAT cross-process determinism docstring overpromises). All MAJOR are FIX-NOW per HARD-RULE-12; none block CI merge.
ground_truth_verify_quality: HIGH — independently traced (a) 7 suites actually built (3 sig arms x 4 enc arms with 5 constructors covering the valid pairings) (b) wrap/unwrap round-trip substantive — `cargo test -p benten-crypto-suite` returned 18 new tests passing including KAT pins with real ML-DSA-65 sig sizes and ML-KEM-768 ciphertext sizes (c) X-Wing combiner verified committing+strip-resistant in `sig.rs` `verify` path via VerifyError::StripResistanceViolated (d) typed-unsupported-fail-closed reachable on dispatcher entry — pin tf4_typed_unsupported_*_codepoint_never_silent_fallback confirms (e) NF-1 PQ⊕PQ buildable — `slh-dsa 0.2.0-rc.5` linked, real sk/vk generated, pure_pq_nf1_kat_self_check() runs sign+verify against live primitives (test takes 10.26s = real SLH-DSA wall-clock) (f) AUDIT_LANDED flag genuinely write-protected — `pub const false` with no setter API, no cfg(test) override, no compile-time-condition (g) 3 R3 RED-PHASE pins genuinely un-ignored (no `#[ignore]` in any of the 3 tf4_*.rs files).

findings.title: 0x647b reserved-for-ML-KEM-768⊕HQC reused for ML-KEM-768-only in SwapMatrix.cipher_suite_codepoint()
findings.evidence: codepoint.rs:190 reserves 0x647b for HYBRID_MLKEM768_HQC (NF-1 ML-KEM-768⊕HQC PQ⊕PQ end-state). cipher_suite.rs:711-715 keeps 0x647b typed-rejected at CipherSuite::resolve. But swap_matrix EncryptionArm::PurePqMlKem768Only (described in docs as 'ML-KEM-768-only; classical X25519 dropped'; lines 179-182) maps to 0x647b. ML-KEM-768-only is NOT the same as ML-KEM-768⊕HQC — the former is a single-PQ stripped-hybrid, the latter is a true PQ⊕PQ hybrid. Even though the audit-landed flag prevents runtime activation today, when the audit flips in v1-GM, callers will see codepoint 0x647b carrying ML-KEM-only payload, not HQC-hybrid payload. Future migration to the true NF-1 HQC arm would either silently break the wire format OR force a re-spend of 0x647b.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW per HARD-RULE-12 (a) since this is the TERMINAL wave before G-CORE-9 freeze. Three resolution options to surface to Ben: (i) mint a new codepoint for 'pure-PQ ML-KEM-768-only' (e.g. 0x647c, separate from the reserved 0x647b HQC end-state); (ii) drop the pure-PQ-enc arm from this wave entirely and defer to FIPS-207 HQC arrival in 2027 (the audit-gate already prevents activation, so the structural surface adds nothing v1-beta-usable); (iii) explicitly document 0x647b's current dual semantic as 'reserved for ML-KEM-768-{only,⊕HQC} disambiguated at audit-flip time' AND name the disambiguation mechanism. Option (i) is the structurally-cleanest; option (ii) is the smallest diff and arguably correct given the wave's safety-invariant framing.

findings.title: KeyMaterial::from_bytes_for_test (test-named API) called from production SwapMatrix::sign_and_seal + open_and_verify hot paths
findings.location: crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/swap_matrix.rs:431, 448, 527, 544 (production-API surfaces — `sign_and_seal` is `pub`, called from non-test consumers per the swap-matrix integration contract)
findings.evidence: aead.rs:103 declares `pub fn from_bytes_for_test(codepoint, bytes: &[u8]) -> Self` with `#[must_use]` and docstring 'Test-only constructor — accept arbitrary bytes + codepoint for per-test K_ROOT vectors.' But `swap_matrix::sign_and_seal` (a `pub fn` production API surface) calls it for the encryption-active arms. The proper API is `from_bytes(codepoint, Vec<u8>)` which is `pub(crate)` — benten-crypto-suite IS the crate, so it COULD call the crate-private constructor. The `_for_test` naming is misleading and trips production-vs-test reviewers (and pim-18 SHAPE-not-SUBSTANCE: a `_for_test` surface in a production hot path is the exact opposite of the discipline).
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW per HARD-RULE-12 (a): rename the 4 call-sites to use `KeyMaterial::from_bytes(codepoint, bytes.to_vec())` (which is `pub(crate)`, in-crate from swap_matrix — works without changing the visibility), OR rename the `from_bytes_for_test` method to drop the `_for_test` suffix and update its docstring (since it's now a real production-arm API). Trivial mechanical fix (<10 LOC). Recommend the rename approach since the existing `from_bytes` takes `Vec<u8>` while `from_bytes_for_test` takes `&[u8]` — they're not API-equivalent.

findings.title: tf4_both_must_verify_strip_pq_half_fails_closed fails at AEAD-AAD layer, NOT NF-4 verify layer
findings.evidence: The test zeros the PQ half of `env.signature_bytes` then calls `hybrid.open_and_verify(...)`. compose_aad (line 1476) includes `signature_bytes` in AAD. At wrap-time AAD was computed over the ORIGINAL signature_bytes; at receive-time the mutated signature_bytes feeds a DIFFERENT AAD. ChaCha20-Poly1305 detects the AAD mismatch as a tag failure and returns `AeadAuthFailed` BEFORE the code reaches the NF-4 verify_payload step. So the test witnesses 'envelope AAD-binding catches sig-mutation' (a real property) but does NOT witness NF-4 strip-resistance (the documented intent — `assert! ... 'MUST fail closed at the NF-4 layer'`). A truly load-bearing NF-4 test would (i) construct a strip-attack payload that flows through the AEAD (e.g. seal with a STRIPPED sig from the start, where the AAD already commits to the stripped form) OR (ii) bypass the AEAD layer and call sig-only verify on a stripped HybridSignature.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW per HARD-RULE-12 (a): tighten the test to actually witness NF-4 strip-resistance, OR rename the test + docstring to honestly say 'fails at AEAD-AAD layer'. Recommend the former since the wave brief calls out NF-4 strip-resistance as a load-bearing safety pin and sig.rs's `verify` path has the StripResistanceViolated arm that should be exercised. Inline trivial fix; orchestrator-direct or a 1-agent follow-up.

findings.title: Pure-PQ encrypt+decrypt paths (pure_pq_mlkem_encapsulate / aead_wrap_pure_pq / aead_unwrap_pure_pq) are structurally unreachable in tests until audit-flag flip
findings.location: crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/swap_matrix.rs:1605-1688 (the 4 helper functions) + 440-465 + 535-554 (the sign_and_seal / open_and_verify pure-PQ branches)
findings.evidence: SwapKeypair::PurePq is only constructable via generate_keypair_for_test when sig_arm == PurePqMlDsa65Slhdsa. SwapMatrix with that sig_arm only comes from try_pure_pq_sole_trust_path which always returns Err(AuditNotLandedPurePqRejected). Therefore no test in the workspace exercises the AEAD wrap+unwrap pure-PQ paths end-to-end. The pure_pq_nf1_kat_self_check witnesses sign+verify only. These primitives could silently break and the regression would not surface until v1-GM audit-flag flip.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW per HARD-RULE-12 (a) via a test-only side-door: e.g. a `#[cfg(test)] fn force_pure_pq_for_test() -> SwapMatrix` that bypasses the audit-flag gate (clearly named, NOT a public surface; only callable from this crate's tests). Pair with end-to-end pure-PQ sign+seal+open+verify pin. This catches FIPS-203 ML-KEM-768 + ChaCha20-Poly1305 integration drift now (cheaply) rather than discovering it during the v1-GM audit window when the cost of fixing-and-re-auditing is much higher.

findings.title: ml_dsa_65_keygen_from_seed_for_test docstring claims 'passing the SAME seed always returns the SAME pubkey bytes' but determinism is only within-process
findings.evidence: The function generates a fresh ML-DSA SigningKey via `MlDsaSigningKey::<MlDsa65>::generate()` (OS RNG) at cache-miss, then caches and returns the result keyed by `seed`. The `seed` is the cache key — NOT input to keygen. A SECOND process starting fresh will populate the cache with a DIFFERENT pubkey for the same seed. The docstring 'passing the SAME seed always returns the SAME pubkey bytes' is true within a single process but false across processes — which is fine for the wave intent (the NF-2 / C-GM-AUDIT will replace this with real NIST KAT vector files) but the docstring overstates the contract.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW per HARD-RULE-12 (a): clarify the docstring to 'within a single process, passing the same seed returns the same pubkey bytes (process-cached synthesis); cross-process determinism arrives via the NF-2 / C-GM-AUDIT real-NIST-KAT-vector fixture'. Trivial inline. Pair this with the existing module-doc comment at lines 1019-1038 which already acknowledges this nuance.

slh_dsa_param_choice_sha2_128s.rationale: The argument that 'codepoint 0x0003 reserves the suite identifier not a parameter set' is structurally correct — the swap-matrix suite-selector dispatches by codepoint, and the underlying SignatureSuite primitive can be re-parameterized internally. The Sha2_128s choice for the conformance-test layer is reasonable (smallest sigs + fastest verify = faster CI). However: the docstring at lines 76-84 says 'wire-format canonical choice (likely upgraded to Sha2_192s for Cat-3 parity) is a G-CORE-9 P-III freeze decision' — but G-CORE-9 will then have to choose between (a) flipping the parameter set under the same codepoint (breaks any v1-beta deployed signatures using Sha2_128s) and (b) minting a new codepoint for Sha2_192s. The docstring should call out this fork explicitly so the G-CORE-9 decision is not surprised by it.
slh_dsa_param_choice_sha2_128s.follow_up: Hardening recommended: add a line to the docstring 'G-CORE-9 P-III freeze must choose: re-parameterize 0x0003 to Cat-3 Sha2_192s (breaks v1-beta deployed pure-PQ sigs — acceptable because pure-PQ-sole-trust-path is structurally non-default until audit flip) OR mint a new codepoint reserving Sha2_128s for the smaller-sig variant'. Trivial inline.

audit_landed_flag_pub_const_no_setter.rationale: Verified via grep: no `set_audit_landed_pure_pq_flag` exists anywhere in the workspace. The constant is declared `pub const AUDIT_LANDED_PURE_PQ_FLAG: bool = false` at module level — no `#[cfg(test)]` override, no compile-time-conditional, no test-only setter API. The `try_pure_pq_sole_trust_path` constructor is the ONLY code path consulting the flag, and it does so via direct `if !AUDIT_LANDED_PURE_PQ_FLAG { return Err(...) }` (line 251). The named typed arm `AuditNotLandedPurePqRejected` is the v1-GM-gating grep target. Workspace test confirms the flag is `false` at baseline (3 separate accessor calls in `tf4_p5b_audit_landed_pure_pq_flag_is_false_at_workspace_baseline`). Flipping the flag requires a future Ben-authored commit modifying the constant value + the gating-side coupled actions (independent audit deliverable + pinned crate versions + sign-off) per the docstring at lines 67-73.
audit_landed_flag_pub_const_no_setter.follow_up: None for the flag mechanic itself. Consider a `#[deny]` lint-style guard at the CI surface in the v1-GM gate cascade so a future commit that flips the flag also has to land the coupled artifacts before merging — but that's a CI infrastructure concern not a code concern, deferrable per the C-GM-AUDIT exit-criterion procedure.
